value.title: Type on the role, the ten definitions and their seed templates (workstream 006 s02)
value.summary: Every role names one of pij's ten seat types. pij ships a definition and a seed template per type; `pij directory add` and `edit` take `--type` and what the type requires; `pij directory types` prints definitions and seeds; a repo edits its own seed copy with a reason.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Every role names one of pij's ten seat types. pij ships a definition and a seed template per type; `pij directory add` and `edit` take `--type` and what the type requires; `pij directory types` prints definitions and seeds; a repo edits its own seed copy with a reason.

sections.name: goals
value: A prime creates a role by naming how it lives, and pij refuses one that names none.
Each type's meaning and seed is printable, and a repo can own its seed copy.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Delivering the type definition or seed to a seat at start: that is PRD 007 s02's first turn, so req-02 and req-08 stay in-progress here.
Showing the type in `pij list` (plan 237) and typing existing roles (plan 238).
Any permission change or daemon enforcement of a type's rules.

value.claim: `pij directory add <id> --why <w>` with no `--type` and no template that supplies one refuses `E-RS-TYPE-MISSING` and lists the ten types, one line each; with `--type knowledge --keeps <artefact>` it writes a role whose `meta.type` is `knowledge`.
A type's required fields are asked for: `--type knowledge` without `--keeps` and `--type steward` without `--sole-writer-of` refuse `E-RS-TYPE-FIELD`, naming the flag.

`pij directory types` lists the ten (id, title, authority, line); `types <type>` prints its purpose, lifecycle, what it keeps, its required fields and its rules, each fixed or default; `types <type> --seed` prints the seed pij would use and names its source (the governance copy `community/seeds/<type>.md`, else the shipped `templates/types/<type>/v1/seed.md`). None of them launches anything.

`--type-change <rule>=<why>` records a change to a default rule in the role's `type_changes`; a fixed rule refuses `E-RS-TYPE-RULE` naming it as fixed, and an unknown rule refuses listing the type's rules. `edit` applies the same checks, and changing `--type` re-checks every recorded change against the new type.
`--type-suggestion <text>` records the type the creator wished existed; the role row in `pij directory --json` carries it as `type_suggestion`.
`add --from template:<name>` takes the template's type from the catalog's template table (or its own `meta.type`); a template with none needs `--type`.

`pij directory seed <type> --from <file> --why <text>` writes `community/seeds/<type>.md` through the single writer, committed with its reason; afterwards `types <type> --seed` names the governance copy.
`--kind` and `--lifecycle` are retired: no longer required or written; given, they are ignored with a warning naming `--type`. A role document written before still reads and validates.

The shipped definitions validate against `pij/type`; the role schema carries `meta.type`, `keeps`, `sole_writer_of`, `type_suggestion` and `type_changes`; `pij directory add --help` and the skill's community references describe types.

value.title: Type on the role, the ten definitions and their seed templates (workstream 006 s02)

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Role documents: crates/daemon/src/community/role.rs (`RoleFields`, `from_fields`, `apply_fields`), the add/edit flag lists in crates/daemon/src/http/directory.rs, and the CLI help in crates/core/src/directory.rs. Role templates are compiled in by crates/daemon/src/community/templates.rs; the type catalog follows the same pattern from templates/types/. Governance writes go through community/writer.rs. Nothing delivers a role's text at assign today (the after-assign hook only drains queued role requests).

value.mitigation: Accepted and ignored with a warning naming --type.

value.risk: Old role documents without a type break the view.
value.mitigation: `type` is optional in the schema; the view shows `type: null`; plan 238 types them.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Cost: on demand only. `types` and `types --seed` read compiled-in bytes and at most one governance file (0 launches). add, edit and seed edits make the single writer's governance commit, the same git and ddocs launches an add makes today. No loop, poll, timer or hook.
No permission rule changes (PRD 003); no daemon enforcement of a type's rules; no existing JSON field removed or renamed.
Builds nice-19 through `just shared-build`, one at a time.
